title: API schema versioning: deprecations, beta headers, backward-compat shims
author: Asha Patel
description: Motivation: As we iterate on the public API surface (streaming semantics, function/tool calling, structured output and OpenAI-compat mappings) we need a clear upgrade path for clients and a short-term compatibility layer to avoid breaking production traffic. This PR introduces: 1) a beta header mechanism (X-Redwood-API-Version) to gate opt-in schema changes; 2) explicit deprecation markings and runtime warnings for fields removed in the upcoming v2 schema; 3) backward-compatibility shims on the server side to translate common v1 request/response shapes into the new internal model; and 4) updates to the OpenAI-compat layer so older OpenAI-shaped requests continue working while emitting deprecation telemetry. Design summary: - Beta header: requests including header "X-Redwood-API-Version: v2-beta" receive the new schema validation and new streaming framing (structured-event enhancements). Production default remains v1 behavior. - Deprecations: fields marked deprecated include "stream_format: legacy_chunk" and top-level "tools" schema variants that used an older function-calling shape. Deprecated fields trigger a warning header "X-Redwood-Deprecation: field=<name>;expires=2026-08-01" in responses when observed. - Backcompat shims: middleware that rewrites legacy OpenAI-compat payloads into the v2 internal representation (and rewrites v2 responses back to v1 shapes for clients not opting in). Shims include KV-cache key normalization, legacy "choices"->new "outputs" translation, and streaming chunk envelope conversion. - Migration notes: document contains a migration checklist and sample transforms in the SDKs (python/typescript). We intentionally avoid breaking changes by default and will flip default to v2 on the scheduled deprecation date after an announced migration window. Testing: unit + integration coverage added for schema transforms, streaming E2E with partial- and full-frame reassembly, and OpenAI-compat request roundtrips. Rollout: feature gated behind the beta header; canary rollout enabled via routing policy config (10% -> 50% -> 100%) with automatic fallback to v1 on errors. See release notes and rollout_plan fields below. Related: ENG-1254 (schema versioning), PM-879 (docs/migration), SUP-4321 (support compatibility spike).

release_notes: Introduces API schema versioning with a beta header (X-Redwood-API-Version) for opt-in v2 behavior; adds deprecation headers and runtime shims to preserve compatibility with OpenAI-shaped requests. Default behavior unchanged. SDKs updated with helper transforms. Admins can opt into v2 via header or routing rules. See docs/api/migration/v2-migration-guide.md for migration steps.
testing: e2e: streaming reassembly with partial and full frames
load: shim overhead microbench + perf budget verified
manual: canary smoke run in us-west-2
rollout_plan: Canary release behind tenant routing: 10% traffic with X-Redwood-API-Version header enabled -> evaluate error/latency/QA -> 50% -> 100% opt-in. Default remains v1 until announced deprecation date (2026-08-01). Automatic fallback to v1 is configured on schema validation errors or runtime panics. Support will be notified and we will publish SDK migration snippets.
notes_for_support: SUP-4321: Provide mapping table for common OpenAI request shapes to v2. Shipping deprecation metric; support can identify top customers using legacy shapes and coordinate migration.
changelog_section: API: introduce v2 beta header, deprecation headers, and compatibility shims (non-breaking default).
